fatal_errors: The hypothesis fails to reconstruct the central controlled comparison: Tb addition to (VNb)0.753(TiHf)0.247 versus the Tb-free starting matrix.
It predicts a generic monotonic VEC–Tc relationship rather than the observed suppression of Tc, upper critical field, heat-capacity jump, and superconducting robustness after Tb addition.
It assumes a single phase with minimal segregation, whereas Tb precipitates, Tb2O3, and probable interfacial concentration gradients are central structural mediators in the target.
The cited studies concern Ta-Nb-based HEAs and do not establish that increasing VEC strengthens electron–phonon coupling or raises Tc in the proposed material class.
Elemental substitution does not isolate VEC because it simultaneously changes mass, phonon spectra, magnetic character, disorder, atomic-size mismatch, and local chemistry.
explanation: The response offers a generic VEC-based alternative rather than reconstructing the reported Tb-addition study. It omits the actual alloy compositions, synthesis and field-dependent calorimetry, secondary phases, quantitative baseline, and observed degradation of superconductivity. Its proposed series and falsification rule are testable in principle, and its phase-stability boundary is reasonable, but XRD confirmation alone would not make VEC the sole controlled variable. E1 supports phonon-mediated superconductivity in a Ta-Nb actinide HEA, while E2 supports dirty-limit isotropic s-wave behavior in Ta-Nb films; neither supports the claimed monotonic increase of electron–phonon coupling and Tc with VEC. Thus the mechanism and predictions are insufficiently evidenced and do not agree with the hidden result.
